expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: canceled variant has only 'cancellation', trialing has only 'trialEndsAt', no field overlap across variants

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: Mentions 'Use exhaustive switches when consuming it' but provides no assertNever implementation or exhaustiveness check code

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: export type SubscriptionId = Brand<string, "SubscriptionId">; export type UtcInstant = Brand<string, "UtcInstant">; export type RetryCount = Brand<number, "RetryCount">;

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Says 'keep status changes behind one transition function' but no implementation provided

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "a canceled subscription cannot accidentally carry retry fields, and a trialing subscription cannot omit its trial end"

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: "Use a discriminated union, not one record full of optional fields"
